title: Generator-filtration homogenization is finite graded and preserves torsion-freeness
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $B$ a commutative $A$-algebra generated by $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and $M$ a $B$-module generated by $m_1,\ldots,m_r$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], where $n,r\geq0$. For $d\geq0$ set $F_dM=\operatorname{span}_A\{b_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots b_n^{\alpha_n}m_j:|\alpha|\leq d,\ 1\leq j\leq r\}$, where $|\alpha|=\sum_i\alpha_i$. Let $N=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}F_dM\,t^d$ be the $A$-module of finite formal polynomials with coefficient of $t^d$ in $F_dM$. Then $F_dM\subseteq F_{d+1}M$, $b_iF_dM\subseteq F_{d+1}M$, and $\bigcup_dF_dM=M$. Put $P=A[X_0,X_1,\ldots,X_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], with each variable of degree $1$. The formulas $X_0(xt^d)=xt^{d+1}$ and $X_i(xt^d)=b_ixt^{d+1}$ define a $P$-module structure on $N$ with internal grading $N_d=F_dM\,t^d$ for $d\geq0$ and $N_d=0$ for $d<0$, satisfying $P_eN_d\subseteq N_{e+d}$. This $P$-module is generated by $m_1t^0,\ldots,m_rt^0$. If $A$ is a domain and $M$ is torsion-free over $A$ (multiplication by every nonzero element of $A$ is injective), then $N$ is torsion-free over $A$.

proof.text: For each $d$, every spanning vector $b^\alpha m_j$ of $F_dM$ is a spanning vector of $F_{d+1}M$, since $|\alpha|\leq d$ implies $|\alpha|\leq d+1$. Multiplication by $b_i$ is $A$-linear and sends this vector to $b^{\alpha+e_i}m_j$, with $|\alpha+e_i|\leq d+1$. Taking finite $A$-linear combinations proves both required inclusions.

source.place: Tag 052N, lemma-homogenize, explicit generator-filtration variant of the module homogenization construction; compare More Algebra Tag 053E, lemma-flat-finite-type-valuation-ring-finite-presentation, proof of (2).

proof.text: By the finite module generators, any $x\in M$ is a finite sum $\sum_jc_jm_j$ with $c_j\in B$. By the algebra generators, each $c_j$ is a polynomial in the $b_i$ with coefficients in $A$. Expand these finitely many polynomials into monomials and choose $d$ at least their finitely many total degrees (take $d=0$ if there are no terms). The resulting expression for $x$ lies in $F_dM$. Thus $\bigcup_dF_dM=M$.

source.place: Tag 052N, lemma-homogenize, explicit generator-filtration variant of the module homogenization construction; compare More Algebra Tag 053E, lemma-flat-finite-type-valuation-ring-finite-presentation, proof of (2).

proof.text: Write $b^\alpha=\prod_{i=1}^nb_i^{\alpha_i}$ and $|\alpha|=\sum_i\alpha_i$. For $k\geq0$ define an $A$-linear operator on finite formal polynomials by $E_{k,\alpha}(\sum_dx_dt^d)=\sum_db^\alpha x_dt^{d+k+|\alpha|}$. This takes values in $N$: expanding $x_d$ in the defining span of $F_dM$, multiplication by $b^\alpha$ raises each spanning monomial degree by $|\alpha|$, so its coefficient lies in $F_{d+|\alpha|}M\subseteq F_{d+k+|\alpha|}M$. The support remains finite. For $p=\sum_{k,\alpha}a_{k,\alpha}X_0^kX^\alpha$ define $p\cdot z=\sum_{k,\alpha}a_{k,\alpha}E_{k,\alpha}(z)$. The unique finite coefficient expansion of a polynomial makes this well-defined.

source.place: Tag 052N, lemma-homogenize, explicit generator-filtration variant of the module homogenization construction; compare More Algebra Tag 053E, lemma-flat-finite-type-valuation-ring-finite-presentation, proof of (2).

proof.text: The operators satisfy $E_{k,\alpha}E_{l,\beta}=E_{k+l,\alpha+\beta}$: on $xt^d$ both sides give $b^{\alpha+\beta}xt^{d+k+l+|\alpha|+|\beta|}$, using commutativity of $B$. Also $E_{0,0}$ is the identity. Expand two polynomials into monomials; their product multiplies coefficients and adds exponents, so this identity gives $(pq)\cdot z=p\cdot(q\cdot z)$. Linearity of every $E_{k,\alpha}$ gives both distributive laws, and the constant polynomial $a$ acts by the existing $A$-scalar $a$. These are the module axioms. The actions of $X_0$ and $X_i$ are exactly the two formulas in the statement.

source.place: Tag 052N, lemma-homogenize, explicit generator-filtration variant of the module homogenization construction; compare More Algebra Tag 053E, lemma-flat-finite-type-valuation-ring-finite-presentation, proof of (2).

proof.text: Every element of $N$ is a finite sum of its terms $x_dt^d$, and if such a sum is zero, every coefficient $x_d$ is zero. Hence the stated $N_d$ give an internal direct-sum grading, extended by zero in negative degrees. A degree-$e$ monomial $X_0^kX^\alpha$ has $k+|\alpha|=e$, so its action takes $N_d$ into $N_{d+e}$ by the displayed formula for $E_{k,\alpha}$. A homogeneous polynomial of degree $e$ is a finite $A$-linear combination of these monomials, proving $P_eN_d\subseteq N_{e+d}$; a negative component is zero.

source.place: Tag 052N, lemma-homogenize, explicit generator-filtration variant of the module homogenization construction; compare More Algebra Tag 053E, lemma-flat-finite-type-valuation-ring-finite-presentation, proof of (2).

proof.text: Each $m_jt^0$ belongs to $N$, since $m_j\in F_0M$. For $|\alpha|\leq d$, the action gives the identity $b^\alpha m_jt^d=X_0^{d-|\alpha|}X^\alpha\cdot(m_jt^0)$. Every coefficient $x_d\in F_dM$ is a finite $A$-linear combination of these $b^\alpha m_j$. Multiplying this expression by $t^d$ and summing over the finite support proves that every element of $N$ is in the $P$-span of $m_1t^0,\ldots,m_rt^0$. This is precisely finite generation.

source.place: Tag 052N, lemma-homogenize, explicit generator-filtration variant of the module homogenization construction; compare More Algebra Tag 053E, lemma-flat-finite-type-valuation-ring-finite-presentation, proof of (2).

proof.text: Assume now that $A$ is a domain and $M$ is torsion-free over $A$. If $0\ne a\in A$ and $a\sum_dx_dt^d=0$ in $N$, equality of formal polynomial coefficients gives $ax_d=0$ in $M$ for every $d$. Torsion-freeness of $M$ gives $x_d=0$ for every $d$, so the original element is zero. Thus multiplication by each nonzero $a$ is injective on $N$, as required.
